output.summary: Crude oil prices rose sharply as Middle East tensions raised fears of supply disruption, with Brent reaching a three-month high. Analysts warn prices could pass $90 by year-end.

Major technology companies reported better-than-expected second-quarter earnings on strong demand for AI infrastructure and cloud services. Some analysts question whether current AI spending is sustainable.

The EU AI Act's transparency requirements came into force, requiring disclosure of AI-generated content and training data sources. Industry groups criticised the timeline while consumer advocates welcomed it.
The central bank held its benchmark rate at 4.25%, citing mixed economic signals. It said rate cuts remain possible in September if inflation keeps falling.
Global renewable energy investment reached a record $380 billion in the first half of 2026, led by solar and wind. Falling technology costs and supportive policy were credited.

A financial services firm disclosed a data breach affecting about 2.3 million customer records, including names, email addresses and encrypted password hashes. The breach exploited an unpatched third-party library.
Automakers announced production slowdowns because of shortages of semiconductors for driver-assistance systems. Third-quarter output is expected to fall by an estimated 150,000 vehicles.
Property prices in Dubai rose 15% in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier. Experts attributed the rise to demand from international investors and an improved regulatory environment.

Several Chinese technology companies announced larger investments in overseas markets, with overseas revenue passing 35% of the total in the first half of 2026. Experts link the trend to growing competitiveness in AI and cloud computing.
MediAssist AI, a healthcare startup specialising in diagnostic imaging, raised $200 million in a Series C round led by Sequoia Capital. It plans to expand into cardiology and neurology.
Delegates at a climate summit in Geneva agreed international standards for carbon credit trading. Environmental groups gave cautious support, saying implementation will decide whether it works.
A large European airline reported a 12% rise in summer bookings despite an 8% increase in average fares. It warned that rising jet fuel costs could pressure margins later in the year.
Two pharmaceutical companies announced a $68 billion merger creating the world's third-largest drug maker by revenue. Regulators are expected to require divestitures before approval.
A CyberWatch International report says ransomware attacks rose 40% in the first half of 2026, with critical infrastructure, healthcare and financial services most targeted.
The professional basketball league confirmed expansion franchises in Mexico City, London, Vancouver and Mumbai, to begin play in the 2028-29 season.
Norway became the first country where electric vehicle sales exceeded combustion engine vehicles for a full quarter, with EVs at 62% of new registrations in Q2 2026.
Markets closed mixed on Friday, with the S&P 500 up 0.3% and the Nasdaq down 0.2% on below-average volume. Bond yields rose on inflation expectations.
A class-action lawsuit alleges that a food delivery platform misclassifies its 140,000 drivers as independent contractors. The company says it will defend its model.
A private space company completed its first commercial orbital flight, carrying four paying passengers for three days. It plans monthly flights by 2027 and lower ticket prices.
International wheat futures fell 5.4% after improved harvest forecasts from major producing regions. The decline brings some relief to food-importing nations.
